title: Book Cover Size: Kindle 1600×2560 px & KDP Paperback Bleed
h1: Book Cover Size for eBooks and Paperbacks
description: Kindle cover size 1600×2560 px per KDP, plus paperback full-wrap PDF rules, 0.125 in bleed, spine width, and why print needs back cover and spine.
summary: For Kindle eBooks, Amazon KDP lists ideal cover dimensions of 1600×2560 px (1.6:1 height to width), JPEG or TIFF, RGB, under 50 MB. Paperback covers must be one PDF with back, spine and front, sized with 0.125 in bleed; PiCraft exports the front panel only.

sections.heading: Kindle eBook cover specs at a glance
paragraphs: These criteria are from Amazon KDP help for eBook cover images. They apply to the JPEG or TIFF you upload to the title.

rows: At least 1.6:1 height to width (1600 px height per 1000 px width)
72 dpi listed; KDP recommends at least 300 PPI for quality

after: Very light or white covers can disappear on Amazon's white detail page. KDP suggests a narrow medium-gray border (about 3–4 px) to show the edges.

sections.heading: Why 1600×2560 px is the practical target
paragraphs: 1600×2560 px hits KDP's ideal size and the 1.6:1 ratio in one file. It is large enough for sharp thumbnails in search and for high-definition devices, while staying far below the 50 MB cap.
Smaller files down to 1000×625 px may upload, but title type and art lose clarity when shoppers see the cover as a small thumbnail. Test readability with the cover scaled to roughly 160 px tall.
KDP applies compression on the store. Avoid heavy JPEG compression before upload; export a clean JPG at full resolution.

sections.heading: KDP paperback cover: full wrap, bleed and spine
paragraphs: A paperback cover on KDP is not a single front panel. It must be one PDF that includes the back cover, spine and front cover as one continuous image.

Bleed on print covers adds 0.125 in (3.2 mm) to the top, bottom and outside edges beyond trim so backgrounds reach the edge after trimming. KDP's cover calculator and templates generate the full width and height from your trim size, page count, paper type and ink choices. To work the numbers out yourself, see [KDP paperback cover size](/sizes/kdp-paperback-cover-size).

Spine width depends on page count and paper (for example, white paper black-and-white interior: page count × 0.002252 in). KDP's help page gives the minimum for spine text as 79 pages in one place and more than 79 in another, so treat 80 pages as the safe minimum. Below 79 pages, leave the spine blank.
Text on the front and back must sit at least 0.125 in inside the trim lines, and spine text needs at least 0.0625 in (1.6 mm) clearance from the spine edges so it does not wrap onto the panels.

sections.heading: 6×9 inch front panel with bleed (PiCraft output)
paragraphs: Many fiction and nonfiction paperbacks use a 6×9 in trim. PiCraft's [Book Cover Maker](/create/book-cover-maker) exports a front-only image at 6.125×9.25 in including bleed on the outer, top and bottom edges (0.125 in beyond the 6×9 trim on those sides), at 300 DPI.

That file is meant to drop into KDP's or another printer's full-wrap template as the front panel. You still need to build the back cover, spine, and optionally a barcode area in the template KDP provides.
Other trim sizes (5×8, 8.5×11, and so on) require different template dimensions. Use KDP's cover calculator for your exact page count rather than resizing the 6×9 front arbitrarily.

sections.heading: Common cover mistakes
items: Uploading only a front JPEG as the entire paperback cover instead of a full-wrap PDF.
Adding spine text on a book with fewer than 79 pages.
Letting title text sit outside the safe area or into the spine zone on a wrap.
Using CMYK or spot colors for an eBook upload that expects RGB JPEG.
Long titles that cannot be read at thumbnail size in Amazon search.
after: Match spelling on the cover to the title metadata exactly. KDP compares cover text to the details you enter during setup.

sections.heading: Make a front cover at KDP-friendly sizes
paragraphs: The [Book Cover Maker](/create/book-cover-maker) produces a 1600×2560 px eBook JPG and a 6×9 in front with bleed for paperbacks. It does not create the spine, back cover or barcode; assemble those in KDP's cover calculator or your designer's template.
For wide creator assets with a different aspect ratio, see [YouTube thumbnail size](/sizes/youtube-thumbnail-size).

faq.q: What size should a Kindle eBook cover be?
faq.a: KDP lists ideal dimensions of 2560 px tall by 1600 px wide, JPEG or TIFF in RGB, with a height-to-width ratio of at least 1.6:1 and file size under 50 MB.

faq.q: What is the minimum eBook cover size on KDP?
faq.a: 1000 pixels in height and 625 pixels in width, still at least a 1.6:1 height-to-width ratio.

faq.q: Does KDP accept only the front cover for paperbacks?
faq.a: No. Paperback covers must be a single PDF including back cover, spine and front. The front file from PiCraft is one panel inside that wrap.

faq.q: How much bleed does KDP require on paperback covers?
faq.a: Add 0.125 in (3.2 mm) bleed to the top, bottom and outside edges of the cover layout beyond trim.

faq.q: When can I put text on the spine?
faq.a: KDP's help page says spine text needs at least 79 pages in one place and more than 79 pages in another, so 80 pages or more is the safe minimum. Cover Creator requires at least 80 pages for spine text.

faq.q: What trim size is the PiCraft paperback front?
faq.a: 6×9 in trim with bleed on the outer, top and bottom edges, exported as 6.125×9.25 in at 300 DPI.
